notes: ACCESS: 1stdibs.com is now behind a Fastly 'embedded challenge' interstitial that the prior Furniture pass did not face - a plain direct fetch returns HTTP 200 with a 13,084-byte JS-challenge document instead of the page. A curl_cffi fingerprint sweep solved it without any proxy: chrome124, chrome131, chrome120 and safari17_0 all get the challenge, while safari18_0 (with a full desktop Accept / Accept-Language / Sec-Fetch-* header set) returns the real 1.0-1.8 MB server-rendered document every time. All ~15 page fetches this session used that profile and every one returned HTTP 200 real content; each result was validated by asserting the challenge marker is absent before parsing. robots.txt was fetched FIRST and DOES name Claude: it carries an explicit 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Crawl-delay: 1' group (no Disallow), i.e. ClaudeBot is allowed with a 1-second crawl delay; the shared probe layer enforces a 2s per-host gap, so that is respected with margin. The global 'User-agent: *' group disallows /search/, /soa/ (except /soa/graphql), /item/, /my/, /checkout/, /similar/, /more-from-seller/ and every '/*<param>=*' faceted URL shape - none of which were requested. Only bare canonical category paths were fetched. TREE: taken from the site's own category facet embedded in each browse page's Relay store (SearchBrowseFilter name=categoryL1/categoryL2/categoryL3/categoryL4, each SearchBrowseFilterValue carrying displayName, urlLabel, a base64 linkReference path, linkable and count) - not from the mega-menu, so nothing reachable only by facet is missed. This matters here: the homepage mega-nav has NO bath entry at all (its 140 links were dumped and grepped for 'bath' - zero hits), yet the facet tree does carry one, so a nav-only walk would have wrongly returned NO BATHROOM FOUND. Furniture is 1stDibs' L1 home department (1,013,590 items). All 13 of its L2 departments were enumerated: Lighting 175,638; Decorative Objects 152,180; Seating 139,089; Tables 122,697; Rugs and Carpets 112,953; Wall Decorations 77,227; Serveware, Ceramics, Silver and Glass 72,969; More Furniture and Collectibles 62,640; Case Pieces and Storage Cabinets 59,300; Building and Garden Elements 30,330; Mirrors 28,542; Asian Art and Furniture 20,592; Folk Art 14,494. Every L2 that could plausibly hold a bathroom node was opened and its full L3 list read: Building and Garden Elements (20 L3s), Mirrors (10 L3s), Case Pieces and Storage Cabinets (18 L3s), More Furniture and Collectibles (6 L3s, plus the L4s under Racks and Stands and Home Accents), Decorative Objects (8 L3s) and Serveware/Ceramics/Silver/Glass (23 L3s). Exactly ONE bathroom node exists in the whole taxonomy: Furniture > Building and Garden Elements > Bathroom Fixtures. DEPTH: Bathroom Fixtures is a true leaf - its page exposes categoryL1/L2/L3 facets and NO categoryL4 facet at all (the same is true of its sibling Architectural Elements, i.e. this department stops at L3), so its own URL is the deepest valid listing URL and may be recorded under rule 24. Building and Garden Elements is a grouping row with blank qty and blank link because it has extractable children. QTY: 756 is the rendered listing header on that exact URL - the 'Search within 756 results' string 1stDibs prints above the grid. It was confirmed three independent ways in the same document: the rendered header, the embedded Relay totalResults value, and the page title 'Antique and Vintage Bathroom Fixtures - 756 For Sale at 1stDibs'. All three agreed to the digit, the <h1> read 'Bathroom Fixtures' and rel=canonical equalled the URL fetched, so there is no silent parent-serving. The page was re-read minutes later and returned 756 again - no session drift. A ?page=2 read returned the same header and 20 further unique item ids, consistent with a 756-item population rather than a first-page cap. Discrimination check: the sibling L3 counts under the same parent run 5,436 / 4,482 / 4,114 / 4,026 / 3,473 / 2,500 / 1,695 / 1,543 / 1,542 / 1,217 / 756 / 692 / 677 / 545 / 452 / 306 / 290 / 130 / 116 / 71, so the number is category-specific, not a site-wide constant. CONTENT CHECK: page-1 titles were read to confirm the node really is bathroom and not a keyword coincidence - 'Italian Carrara Marble Neoclassical Bathroom Pedestal Sink Basin', 'Marblecolors Washbasin by Serafini', 'Early 1900s Antique Free Standing Italian Marble Bathtub', 'Copper Bathtub Bath', 'French Neoclassical Revival Chrome Toilet Tissue Holder', 'Ceramic and brass toilet brush holder with toilet paper holder', 'Zante towel holder with brass dolphins', 'Argentella Bath Set'. That is basins, bathtubs, toilet-roll and toilet-brush holders and towel holders - squarely rules 4, 5, 13, 14 and 17. EXCLUDED and why: Stone Sinks (452) -> review, genuinely ambiguous (see the review entry). Mirrors L2 (28,542) and all 10 of its L3s (Wall Mirrors, More Mirrors, Floor and Full-Length, Table, Mantel/Fireplace, Pier/Console, Sunburst, Convex, Trumeau, Girandoles) - these are general decorative and antique mirrors with no bathroom or vanity-mirror node anywhere beneath them, so under rules 2, 11 and 29 they stay in the Mirrors category and are NOT re-cut as Bathroom. Case Pieces and Storage Cabinets (Cabinets, Cupboards, Apothecary Cabinets, Linen Presses...) - general antique case furniture, no bathroom vanity node. Racks and Stands L4 (Coat, Magazine, Umbrella, Hat, Easels, Music, Luggage) and Home Accents L4 (Screens, Bookends, Trunks, Obelisks, Globes, Ladders, Bird Cages) - contain no towel-rack or bath node. Decorative Objects and Serveware/Ceramics/Silver/Glass - no bath accessory node (the ceramics there are tableware, which rule 18 does not pull into Bathroom). Lighting L2 - no bathroom-lighting node exists, so nothing had to be routed out to Lighting from this site. The /style/, /material/, /origin/, /period/, /creator/ and ?item-type= facet paths were ignored throughout: they are filter re-cuts of the same inventory, not categories (e.g. bathroom-fixtures exposes style and material facets whose linkable paths are /furniture/.../style/<x>/), and recording them would double-count.

review.issue: AMBIGUOUS - LOW CONFIDENCE (rule 29), NOT recorded as a row: Furniture > Building and Garden Elements > Stone Sinks. Carved-Stone Water Trough' and 'Antique Spanish Stone Basin or Planter'. The site's own facet cross-counts confirm the mixture: of the 452, only 53 also carry Bathroom Fixtures while 46 also carry Planters and Jardinieres, 39 Fountains and 9 Garden Ornaments. Site hierarchy places it under Building and Garden Elements next to Fountains and Planters, not under a bathroom node, so it is sent to review rather than guessed either way.
